summary.intent: Run the GSD gap-closure workflow to plan and execute fixes for Phase 68's two ROT-07 verification gaps, then, after the user demanded a full local web-e2e run (not just the rotation suite), diagnose why it fails and scope the follow-up work needed to make it pass.
summary.outcome: Phase 68 gap closure (plans 68-11, 68-12) was planned, verified, executed, and re-verified clean (14/14 must-haves, ROT-07 live). The full web-e2e suite was run locally and failed structurally (6/208 passed) because the v2.0 web app's read/write runtime is stubbed since Phase 62/63/65 (46 'not implemented' stubs); a new Phase 68.1 was scoped, researched, and planned (13 plans across 6 waves) to wire the web app to the existing sdk-core read/write chain, with the plan-checker finding one blocker (kind-cache never wired) currently being revised before execution.

repo: GSD gap-closure mode (`--gaps`) reads VERIFICATION.md 'failed' truths, skips research, and appends new plan numbers (e.g. 68-11+) without touching existing plans.
GSD's commit-helper tool has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log`, never blindly retry.

For single-plan sequential waves that share a modified file (e.g. both touching client.ts), skip worktree isolation and run executors sequentially on the main branch — avoids merge risk and matches prior user feedback that worktrees give no benefit there.

GSD's `close_phase_todos` step will retire ALL todos tagged `resolves_phase: N` on phase completion, even ones NOT actually resolved by a gap-closure run — must inspect each todo's frontmatter/content before letting it auto-close.
`gsd-tools phase insert <N>` / `next-decimal <N>` cleanly inserts a decimal phase (e.g. 68.1) between existing phases without renumbering later phases — safer than hand-editing ROADMAP.md.

Playwright's `webServer` config auto-starts the mock-IPNS-routing (:3001), API dev (:3000), and web dev (:5173) servers itself; external infra (Postgres :5432, Kubo :5001/8080, Redis) must already be running, and `tests/web-e2e/.env`'s `BASE_URL` must point to localhost or Playwright skips starting servers entirely.

A running `nest start --watch` API process respawns instantly on the port it was watching — env vars are loaded at process boot and not refreshed on source-only file changes, so a long-running watch process can hold stale config even though on-disk .env files are correct.
SC#5 doctrine in this repo: zero unit tests under `apps/web/src/**/*.spec.ts` — web behavior must be proven via Playwright web-e2e specs, with SDK-level logic covered by Vitest.

The v2.0 milestone was built plumbing-first: entire behavioral paths (login/root-init, navigation, file preview/download/streaming, shared-folder read, most write ops) are deliberately stubbed with `not implemented — phase 63` / `phase 65` throws until their owning integration phase lands — this is expected architecture, not a bug, per PROJECT.md's stated approach (D-01).

`SealedChildRef` (the v3 read-chain schema) deliberately has no `kind` field, so the web app cannot distinguish file vs. folder children without either a network hop per child or a load-time kind cache — a real architecture decision, not an oversight.

Owned `FolderState` (packages/sdk/src/types.ts) lacks the `writeKey`/`publishedNode` fields that `SharedFolderState` carries — owned subfolder/file write-chain support requires extending the owned model to mirror the shared write-body model, since v3 dropped `SealedChildRef.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted`.

code.finding: New-user login throws 'not implemented — phase 63' before publishing the root Node, blocking the entire login→vault flow; introduced by commit b2dba554a (Phase 62, 'unified Node codec and two-key vault v3 blob'), predates Phase 68.

`ensureFolderLoaded` is dead code (throws 'not implemented — phase 63'); the real live pre-mutation resolve gate is `reconcileFolderSequence`, called before every rename/delete/deleteToBin/move — this is where the fail-closed `enforceResolved` gate was actually wired (plan 68-11).

`rotateReadFromNode` previously returned void, discarding the root's rotated {readKey, generation, sequenceNumber}; its only production caller is `performScopeExitRotation` at client.ts:569, so changing the return type to `RotateReadResult | undefined` was backward-compatible (plan 68-12) and let folderTree self-heal after scope-exit rotation.

Canonical, fully-implemented write-chain reference (createSharedSubfolder, uploadToSharedFolder, updateSharedFile, moveInSharedFolder, deleteFromSharedFolder, updateSharePermission) — the template the Phase 68.1 planner copied from to build the missing owned-file write-chain and wire shared-write client/web handlers.

workflow: When re-verifying a phase after gap closure, distinguish 'proven by live test execution' from 'proven by spec authored + registered' — Playwright specs passing `--list` and typecheck is not the same as the suite actually running green; state this distinction explicitly rather than letting a passed verification imply full runtime coverage.

Before declaring a stale process/port a blocker, check whether a dev watcher (nest --watch, vite, etc.) is already serving current source — reusing a live, verified-current dev server is lower-risk than killing someone's watch setup.

When a big scope gap is discovered mid-task (e.g. web-e2e failing due to unrelated stubbed runtime), pause to research/inventory before proposing a new phase — dispatch parallel inventory agents (read-chain vs write-chain) to establish whether the gap is 'wire to existing primitives' (tractable) vs 'build from scratch' before committing to a plan size.

friction: Config conflict between `auto_advance: true` and `mode: interactive` required an explicit user confirmation before launching the execute-phase run, since the plans touched security-sensitive fail-closed crypto code.
GSD's commit-helper reported a false `commit_failed` twice during this session, requiring manual `git log` verification each time to confirm the commit actually landed.
Docker reported the mock-ipns-routing container as 'unhealthy' even though it was actually serving correctly (records:20) — the health flag was misleading.

A stale API process (18h old, pre-dating today's Phase 68 API route) occupied :3000; killing it caused a `nest --watch` parent to instantly respawn a new process on the same port, requiring extra investigation to confirm it was current before reuse.

The full web-e2e suite run took ~22.7 minutes and returned exit code 0 from the wrapper script despite the underlying Playwright run failing (`EXIT=1`) — the wrapper's own final echo masked the real failure, requiring a second read of the log to catch it.

Discovered mid-session that making the full web-e2e suite pass is not a Phase 68 gap at all but requires an entirely new phase of work (46 stubbed runtime call sites across read + write chains) — a scope surprise that expanded the task substantially beyond the original gap-closure request.

Plan-checker caught a blocker in the newly-planned Phase 68.1 (13 plans): the D-02 kind-cache (`resolveKinds`) was defined but never actually wired into any folder-load/navigation path, meaning every file would render as a folder — required a revision iteration before execution can proceed.
open_items: Phase 68.1 plan revision (iteration 1/3) is in progress to add the missing `resolveKinds` wiring task before the plan-checker can re-verify and execution can begin.

4 todos tagged `resolves_phase: 68` were deliberately NOT auto-closed because they were not resolved by the Phase 68 gap closure — they need user retriage/retagging to a rotation-hardening or write-plane phase (rotation-concurrent-add-merge-downgrades-rotated-child-readkey, rotation-fresh-record-resume-and-sc4-double-bump, rotation-coderabbit-followups-deferred, phase68-shared-write-context-publishednode-wiring).
`.planning/PROJECT.md`'s 'Current State' narrative is ~5 phases stale (still references 'Next: Phase 63') — left untouched as pre-existing milestone-level drift, not addressed this session.
The full local web-e2e suite still does not pass — that is now the explicit exit gate for the newly created Phase 68.1, not yet executed.

Phase 68.1's two architecture decisions (D-02 kind discrimination via load-time cache, D-03 extending owned FolderState with a write-body) were resolved by the planner with recommendations but still await explicit user review/approval before execution proceeds.
